title: Streaming client disconnect heuristics, adaptive backpressure, and partial generation indexing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: client disconnects and slow clients are a significant source of wasted GPU cycles and KV cache divergence. When a client disconnects mid-generation we need a robust strategy to reclaim resources, preserve resumability where possible, and avoid polluting prefix caches with partial or inconsistent keys. Goals: 1) Implement an adaptive backpressure heuristic that detects slow/lagging consumers and throttles batching to preserve SLOs for healthy clients; 2) Introduce a partial-generation indexing scheme so resumed requests can reconcile partial outputs without replaying entire prefix computations; 3) Provide clear abort and cleanup paths that minimize resource waste while retaining useful resume tokens for short-lived reconnects; 4) Maintain compatibility with current function-call/structured-output flow and SDK expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive backpressure reduces GPU token waste by >= 35% for simulated slow-client workloads in our perf harness
Partial-generation index enables resume success for >= 95% of reconnects within a 60s grace period
No breaking API changes for existing SDK streaming or function-call users
Automated test coverage for disconnect scenarios and cache reconciliation in CI
Monitoring dashboards show per-client token waste, resumed success rate, and reclaimed resource counts
design_decisions: Use soft-lease time windows (configurable per-customer tier) to define reconnect grace periods instead of hard TTLs
Index partial generations by (session_id, generation_epoch, last_emitted_token_offset) and store lightweight reconciliation manifests separate from KV cache shards
Prefer conservative KV cache trimming on abort: mark entries as stale and allow background compaction rather than immediate eviction to support quick reconnects
Adaptive backpressure based on three signals: per-connection ack latency, token consumption variance, and queue buildup across runtime shards
Expose per-connection urgency and health as metrics to the console to let customers tune policies
implementation_plan: 1) Add generation manifest store schema and APIs (read/write) with small metadata payloads; keep manifests compressed and size-limited
2) Implement lease manager: issue soft leases on active generations, extend on heartbeat/ack, and publish lease events to coordinator
3) Instrument runtime to emit connection health signals and implement backpressure controller that can reduce batch sizes or deprioritize work for lagging streams
4) Implement partial-index reconciliation flow in resume endpoint: lookup manifest, validate KV prefix slices, and compute minimal re-run segments
5) Add GC worker that compacts stale manifests and marks KV slices eligible for eviction after configurable grace windows
6) End-to-end integration tests and load tests in staging using the perf harness and synthetic slow-client scenarios
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag stream.backpressure.v2 initially off for all customers
Canary rollout to 5% of host-API traffic with tight SLO monitoring for two weeks
Opt-in beta for dedicated customers with ability to configure grace windows and urgency thresholds
Full enable when metrics show stable or improved latency and token-efficiency across samples
Docs and SDK changelog published before full rollout; provide migration guide for private deployments
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest read/write and lease expiration logic
Integration tests that simulate disconnects at different offsets and validate resume success rates
Load tests with mixed fast and slow clients to quantify token waste and latency impacts
Chaos test: random broker restart and simulated network partitions while reconnects occur
Regression tests ensuring function-call structured outputs are preserved during resume (no corrupted JSON payloads)
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboard: Streaming Efficiency - token_waste_ratio, resumed_success_rate, soft_lease_extensions
Alert: resumed_success_rate < 90% over 5m for customer-tier PROD
Alert: token_waste_ratio increases by >50% vs baseline over a sliding 15m window
Trace-level sampling for resume flows to surface edge-case mismatches
SLO report integrated into Console per-model and per-route
